questions.question: Define etiquette in sport and give two examples of etiquette in a named sport.

points.text: Etiquette in sport refers to the unwritten rules, conventions and customs that govern behaviour and show respect for others. It is not enforced by officials but is expected by the sporting community. Two examples in cricket: (1) The fielding team claps a batter who reaches a milestone (50 or 100 runs). questions.question: Explain the difference between sportsmanship and gamesmanship, using sporting examples.

points.text: Sportsmanship is playing fairly and within the spirit of the sport, showing respect for opponents and the rules. Gamesmanship is bending the rules to gain an advantage without actually breaking them. Example of sportsmanship: A golfer calls a penalty on themselves when their ball moves, even though no one else saw it. questions.question: What is the contract to compete and why is it important for fair competition?

points.text: The contract to compete is the unwritten agreement between all participants that they will compete within the agreed rules, give their best effort, and respect officials' decisions. It is important because without this agreement, competition has no meaning - if some participants are cheating, not trying, or ignoring rules, the contest is not fair or genuine. questions.question: A football team is winning 1-0 in the last 5 minutes and starts time-wasting. Is this gamesmanship or cheating? Explain your answer.

points.text: This is gamesmanship rather than cheating because the team is bending the rules rather than breaking them. Time-wasting exploits the rules (no specific time limit on restarts) rather than violating them directly. questions.question: How does gamesmanship undermine the contract to compete? Explain with reference to a specific example.

points.text: Gamesmanship undermines the contract to compete because it violates the spirit of the agreement even if it follows the letter.
